sectors.trend: Iron ore prices under pressure ('roaches seethe'); gold sector active with Forrestania PFS and Aurum Côte d'Ivoire discovery; LNG exports to Japan surging while domestic East Coast supply tightens
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face near-term headwinds from soft iron ore; gold names (WPM.AX, NGN.AX, FOR.AX) benefit from discovery pipeline; energy names (WDS.AX, GSO.AX) see mixed signals from LNG demand vs domestic supply

sectors.trend: Big four banks advanced on easing yields; RBA warning and IMF spending-cut call signal further tightening; recession odds rising
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from wider NIMs if rates rise, but credit risk and loan growth concerns mount with 2027 recession probability increasing

sectors.trend: Petrol price shock hitting consumers; Middle East oil shock risk elevated; Victoria retreats from renewable transmission; coal policy under political pressure
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) face domestic supply constraints; renewable developers (ARE.AX, LNC.AX) hit by Victoria policy reversal; coal (BRL.AX, WES.AX) sees political headwinds

sectors.trend: Coles criticised for milk pricing; Qantas strike threat; EV adoption accelerating; visa changes threaten food security
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CBA.AX (retail banking) face margin pressure; QAN.AX strike risk is near-term negative; food security concerns weigh on CSL.AX-adjacent agribusiness

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn Queensland datacentre deal; AI job displacement debate; ASX small-caps (Latrobe, CurveBeam, Arrow, Sultan) outperforming
sectors.implications: Datacentre/infrastructure plays (SGH.AX, VMC.AX) benefit; ASX tech small-caps show relative strength; AI capex cycle supports long-term demand

sectors.trend: Housing 'absurdly unaffordable'; tenants see modest rent relief; no major REIT-specific headlines
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy pressure from affordability crisis; residential REITs may see tenant turnover risk

key_themes: RBA tightening cycle vs recession risk – policy dilemma intensifying
Commodity divergence: iron ore weak, gold strong, LNG bifurcated
Energy transition policy inconsistency (Victoria renewables retreat vs coal politics)
AI/datacentre capex as new ASX growth vector
Consumer squeeze: petrol, milk, housing affordability
Global macro fragility: Buffett exit, 'four horsemen' narrative, Middle East oil risk

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / IMF fiscal tightening
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; reduce leverage; favour rate-sensitive banks with strong capital buffers
Maintain defensive allocation (staples, healthcare, utilities); avoid cyclical overexposure

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / petrol price spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; monitor WDS.AX, STO.AX; consider fuel-cost-linked consumer hedges
Reduce QAN.AX exposure pre-strike; monitor travel-sector sentiment
Monitor NAB.AX, ANZ.AX loan-loss provisions; underweight residential REITs
Reduce BHP.AX, FMG.AX weight; rotate into gold (WPM.AX, NGN.AX)

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners on discovery pipeline and safe-haven demand
opportunities.rationale: Forrestania PFS and Aurum high-grade discovery signal sector upside; recession hedging demand supports gold

opportunities.recommendation: Add datacentre/infrastructure exposure on Anthropic $31bn Queensland deal
opportunities.rationale: Structural AI capex cycle; Queensland site creates local supply-chain and REIT opportunities

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical long big four banks on rate-hike expectations
opportunities.rationale: Wider NIMs if RBA hikes; banks already advancing; but cap position size given recession risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / thermal coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore under pressure; coal policy risk in Victoria; commodity divergence unfavourable

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim QAN.AX ahead of strike; rotate to defensive consumer
defensive_moves.rationale: Industrial action risk is binary and near-term; WES.AX, WES.AX staples offer stability
RBA hike + IMF fiscal tightening + recession odds rising create uncertain backdrop

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to mildly negative over next 1–3 months. RBA decision is the dominant catalyst; a hike would pressure growth and property names but support bank NIMs. Oil volatility and Qantas strike add noise. Volatility elevated after 'limping' week.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious. Rising 2027 recession odds, IMF fiscal warnings, and housing affordability stress cap upside. Gold, healthcare (CSL.AX), and datacentre infrastructure offer structural growth. Iron ore and coal face structural headwinds. AI capex cycle is a positive offset.

Buffett/Berkshire succession impact on global risk appetite
